name: attacker-writes-manifest
why: a non-install process writing a pod manifest into /etc/kubernetes/manifests/ is the static-pod persistence primitive (TRR9003 Procedure A)
source: recorded via source: atomics/T1543.005/src/emulate.sh writes the manifest with `sh -c 'cat > $dst'`; on Debian-based kind nodes /bin/sh is dash, so the creating process (the shell's O_CREAT|O_TRUNC redirection, before cat execs) is /usr/bin/dash, not cp

name: invalid-namespace-ghost-manifest
why: the invalid-namespace evasion writes the same directory from a non-install process; the file-event node sensor catches the variant the API-server mirror-create misses. The file is created by the shell's `cat >` redirection (dash on kind nodes), not by cp
source: recorded via source: emulate.sh node_put_manifest for the gap variant -- docker exec sh -c 'cat > $dst'; the O_CREAT is the dash process, verified by strace of `sh -c 'cat > f'`

name: writes-pki-not-manifests
why: a write to /etc/kubernetes/pki (an adjacent control-plane dir) does not fire: it shares the /etc/kubernetes parent but not the manifests path. The rule has a single selection item (the manifests dir), so a write outside it shares no positive item and is a benign sanity floor, not a near-miss (there is no second selection to keep while breaking the path)
source: synthetic: a non-install process writing a cert under /etc/kubernetes/pki

name: kubeadm-bootstrap-manifest
why: kubeadm writes the control-plane static-pod manifests during bootstrap; the Image allowlist (endswith /kubeadm) alone must suppress it

name: dpkg-installs-kubelet-keep
why: the only thing the kubelet .deb ships into /etc/kubernetes/manifests/ is the empty marker .kubelet-keep (dpkg unpacks it, writing .kubelet-keep via its .dpkg-new temp); kubeadm, not dpkg, generates and upgrades the real manifests. dpkg creating .kubelet-keep matches the selection and the Image allowlist (endswith /dpkg) alone must suppress it
source: recorded via source: kubernetes/release cmd/krel/templates/latest/kubelet/kubelet.spec:59 touch .../manifests/.kubelet-keep, shipped in the kubelet .deb; dpkg unpacks it on the node

name: dpkg-writes-tmp-file
why: a dpkg write to /tmp cannot fire even if the path matched, because dpkg is in the install filter: a sanity floor that stays quiet
source: synthetic: dpkg writing a scratch file under /tmp during a package operation

name: dropper-named-kubeadm-writes-manifest
why: a dropper named kubeadm outside kubeadm's install path that writes a pod manifest fires: the install filter is pinned to full paths, so the last path element no longer suppresses it
source: synthetic: create of a manifest in /etc/kubernetes/manifests/ by /tmp/kubeadm

name: dropper-named-dpkg-writes-manifest
